newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsuzuka says received donations from oil dealer.
newsitem.headline: Mitsuzuka says received donations from oil dealer.

text.p: Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Tuesday that he had received political donations from oil dealer Junichi Izui, but said that the donations were legal and proper.
He confirmed media reports that had quoted an LDP official as saying on Monday that Mitsuzuka's LDP faction received 6.5 million yen from Izui over a two-year period starting in 1992.
Izui was arrested last week on suspicion of evading 310 million yen in taxes.

Mitsuzuka said he was following through on a pledge he made when he became finance minister to reveal details of any political contributions from Izui after faction officials had looked into the matter.
"We hadn't been asked to do anything (in return for Izui's political donations)," he said. "It was not a donation of that sort."
Asked if these donations were legal, he said: "I have received reports that they have been dealt with appropriately and that there are no problems with them."
Mitsuzuka said he received political donations from Izui after he became head of his LDP faction in 1991.

With Japanese newspapers reporting that Izui made donations to some of the nation's key politicians, his tax evasion case has taken on political overtones and proved an embarrassment for Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's new minority government which was formed only last week.
